verdict:
Joki is accurate to the plans and runs fast, but it is not yet at the million-euro bar. It is a big step up from the old scene. The Showroom now uses the correct SPEC geometry: LED wall at r 8.45, counters at J 186.7/218/250/281/312/341°. All nine tower stands, the 33 Aula and 42 Cave tables, the amphitheatre and the 448-element fin ring with its two cut-outs are correct, and so is the cordoned street door with the rainbow stair. The Showroom is close to convincing, with a logo above every counter, the zig-zag LED ceiling and black counters with stools. Engineering is solid: 60 fps on high and ultra, 0 module or console errors, 0 flights through buildings and no missing targets. What breaks the illusion is the following:
- **Fins by day:** the tower's signature fin screen looks like a mottled frosted curtain, because of shadow-map aliasing (confirmed by toggling the fins' received shadows).
- **Fins at night:** the fins become an overexposed peach lampshade.
- **Aula:** dim and grey, about 1.5 stops darker than the bright white Aula in the photos.
- **Company Lounge:** tinted orange, so the concrete reads as plywood.
- **Floors 2–3:** still look like a CG mock-up: light-grey core with placeholder doors, one white plastic duct, white tile ceiling, cardboard-coloured seating steps, and a stair that rises into the air in the floor-2 cut-away.
- **Ease of use:** the default Joki view cuts off the Showroom, and BioCity hides part of it. The Aula target is half hidden behind BioCity, and the Showroom view leaves out counter 1. Floor-1 labels show through walls in the Showroom and on the routes. In walk mode the lift offers only one destination, the roof walkway is treated as being inside floor 2, and the cut-away stays open when you orbit down to eye level.

All screenshots referenced below are in <scratch>/jokiqa/.

From the street, BioCity is the strongest part of the twin. The black ribbon facades on Lemminkäisenkatu, the glass corner tower with SCIENCE PARK, the Tykistökatu recess with its silver atrium gable, crown bridge, flags and supercars, and the lit offices and glowing atrium at dusk and night all read as real at 15:30, 16:45, 18:00 and 01:00. At 15:30 the eye-level build hall with about 280 seated builders is convincing. The plumbing is sound: chase-mode tours work; all four int-bio route legs walk at 99% with 0 m floor error; 0 of 756 audited flights pass through a building; no module or console errors from the twin itself; 60 fps on the M2 at high and ultra (410–513 draws, 1.3–1.56 M triangles). What still breaks the million-euro illusion:

1. **Partner arrival on foot fails.** Walk mode from the Tykistökatu entrance starts 11° off the door axis. The walker slides along the gable glass into the recess corner and gets stuck.
2. **Eye-level tour shows the avatar.** It sits as a beige diamond in every frame.
3. **Daytime and night hall.** On Saturday at 11:00 the hall is a white haze and looking up is pure white. At night the upper atrium is black.
4. **Dollhouse problems.**
   - A grey roof slab hides the stair down to Joki.
   - Lift-tower braces stick out above the cut.
   - Stand labels are missing or clipped exactly in the "Partner stands" view.
5. **Courtyard (builders' entrance) looks like a placeholder.**
   - A plain concrete cube stands in front of the entrance.
   - The "timber" terrace looks snow-white.
   - The auditorium wall is blank, with no mural.
   - The path is unlit after dark.
6. **Joki-facing SE end is a featureless black wall.** No glass field and no duct cylinders.
7. **Revolving door reads as a white gazebo.**
8. **Joki has no ceiling where the passage stair arrives.** You see the sky through it.

Most fixes are local: the walk start and its heading, layer assignment, materials, exposure adaptation and label priority. Fixing the 1 critical and 9 high items would bring BioCity close to the owner's bar. Accuracy against the plans (stands, tables, recess, columns, entrances) is already good.

The campus exterior is now an accurate, convincing architectural model, but not yet "million-euro" and not yet effortless. Massing and terrain check out against the 2022 and 2025 orthophotos and the KartaView street photos: LOD2 heights, the EduCity deck at +3.40, Lemminkäisenkatu's fall, the Joki levels, kerbs, lanes and lamp masts. Several hero moments are close to photoreal: the Tykistökatu recess with the procedural G-Classes, Joki's fin drum from the NE deck, BioCity's vault and black ribbon facades, the Ströget deck and the EduCity Main Stairs. Daytime streets at 11:00 hold up well. There were no console or module errors in any run, and the flight audit is clean (0 of 756 flights through buildings). It runs at 60 fps on high and ultra at 1280×800 (at most 471 draw calls and 1.34 M triangles). It falls short in four ways. First, wayfinding fails in the overview: BioCity has no building label at all. Its partner and builder entrances, EduCity registration and door B are hidden by occlusion, while a closed Joki door is the most prominent entrance label (on phones without the word "closed"). Second, the train arrival shows Kalevansilta and the platform canopies built twice. Third, recurring CG giveaways break the illusion: low-poly traffic cars and a box-like bus, regular leaf-dot lattices in trees, a SimCity-style far-city band in every aerial, streaky pink EduCity brick, chain-link-like solar roofs, a flat teal Electrocity wall, milky low-contrast daylight, dusk that renders as night, and sodium-orange lighting at night. Fourth, the first visit to each area freezes the frame for up to about 1.5 s while shaders compile. Fixing the two critical label issues, the duplicated structures, the traffic and tree artefacts, the far field and the compile freeze would take this area from a convincing model to near-photoreal and genuinely easy for partners.

The daytime and low-sun looks are close to photoreal. The sun is correct for Turku: engine stats match SPEC §8.1 to 0.01° at every preset. 15:30 has warm SW-facing tops over shaded streets, 16:20 has a believable pink sunset glow, and 16:45 is a good blue hour with lamps and windows coming on. Changing time is technically solid: setTime takes ≤6 ms and the PMREM rebuild about 25–30 ms over 2 frames. Dragging the slider at the UI's 120 ms throttle never produced a frame gap over 16.8 ms. A static camera showed no flicker (0.00 MAD), interiors scrub smoothly, and there were no console errors or module errors on high, ultra or mobile low. The draw-call drop at about 16:26 is only the sun's shadow pass stopping, not a visible pop. The illusion breaks after dark and at a few specific moments. Night is lit by a strong uniform warm ambient (a 5 lux hemisphere light plus a night sky of about 0.4–2 cd/m²), so it reads as sepia "day-for-night": lamp pools on Tykistökatu are invisible and white facades glow beige. The image even gets brighter from 17:30 to 20:00. Opened-building views (Joki, EduCity, BioCity) turn their surroundings into a black void at night. The low-sun exposure jumps by about 0.6 EV in a single frame on the default 15:30 arrival routes into the sun. The overview's far ground shows huge radial light/dark curtains at Saturday 11:00 and Sunday 13:00. BioCity's ground-floor glazing and EduCity's windows become flat white panels at night. EduCity stays fully lit at 01:00 although it is closed, and pedestrians teleport whenever the time changes. All are fixable in the owning modules. Fixing the first five issues below would move the night presets from "rendered" to "photographed".

EduCity is accurate where it counts and recognisable from every side: the stepped terraces, inclined brick top, plant room, glass pavilion with its three skylights, door B portal, Main Stairs and ICT-City bridges are all there. All 4 educity:* views and all 24 targets resolve (missingTargets = [], 15 rooms, 5 areas, 4 entrances). There were no module errors and no twin console errors. Budgets hold: EduCity is roughly ≤60 draws / ≈136k tris on low and ≈230k tris on high, 60 fps steady, with view-switch hitches ≤100 ms. It does not yet look like a million euros. The Kolumba brick renders 40–60 % too dark and too cold: flat black paint from the street, a black/white barcode up close. The windows have none of the sky reflection that defines the real facade. Interiors look beige/peach, wash to flat white from outside at dusk, and sun patches show halftone dither. Upside-down floor-1 furniture shows through the Joukahaisenkatu shopfront. Ease of use breaks at the most important places. In walk mode you cannot enter either main entrance: at the west door you fall about 3.9 m under the pavilion, and the east door has an invisible wall. The lobby has no south-west wall from inside. The Registration and Main-entrances views frame blank slabs or clip their labels. Phones show no Registration, Team formation, Taidon portaat or Kisälli labels. Fix the 2 criticals and the brick, glass and light highs first; the rest is polish.

I tested all 12 TOURS_3D routes and walk mode. The tours: 8 seeks per tour, 1,212 analysed samples, real-time playback with per-frame camera tracking, and Walk-me-there and reduced-motion runs. Walk mode: 30 keyboard-driven scenarios in BioCity, Joki, EduCity and outdoors, plus pure collider checks (flood fill and a 0.3 m sweep) on the modules' own walk data. In daylight, mid-route, the tours already look like a polished product. The ribbon is clean (no z-fighting, it rides the stair nosings and narrows to a guide line at doors), captions change at the right spots on every route, every tour ends on the correct target card, and the frame rate is 60 fps on the high tier (≤ 512 draw calls, ≤ 1.48 M triangles). Walk mode indoors feels right: eye height is 1.64–1.65 m, no walls were walked through, and Go down to Joki, Joki floor 1→2 and the EduCity step-free lift all work. The illusion breaks at the moments partners and builders care about most. On the train arrival the chase camera sits inside or under the roof of the covered Kalevansilta footbridge and its stair (≈13 s per train tour). The camera snaps 5–7 m at almost every door, and several routes open with the camera inside a building. The avatar sinks into the EduCity outdoor Main Stairs and walks through glass, a concrete planter, a vestibule wall and the revolving door's centre post. In walk mode you cannot walk up the ramp from the Joki Aula to the Showroom, and you sink through the deck at EduCity's main entrances. Indoors at night the avatar is a black silhouette, and first-person view shows the avatar's own head. On phones the route card covers the avatar. My estimate is that the area is about 70 % there: the data and the ribbon are strong, and the camera, avatar grounding and door geometry need one focused pass.
